meta.title: The Way from the Bus Stop

paragraphs: My name is Tom, and I am twelve years old. Uncle Dan is Dad's older brother, and he comes to see us on Saturday. He lands at the airport at ten o'clock in the morning. Then he takes the bus into the town. Dad has to work, so I write the directions for Uncle Dan. He does not know our street very well. I want to make the way as easy as I can. The walk is short. It takes ten minutes.

Get off the bus at the stop next to the university. Stand with the university gate behind you. Walk straight along the road for two minutes. You will see the fire station on the left. Do not walk past it. The station is red and white. Turn left at the fire station into a small street. The big road is busy, and the traffic there is worse in the morning. Please do not walk on it.

There is not much traffic on the small street. Walk to the shop at the end, and cross the street at the crossing. Then walk as far as the green gate. Our house is the last house before the park. It has a red door and a small garden. You cannot miss it. Pip will be at the gate. He will bark when he sees you.

Is the way easy, Uncle Dan? If you are lost, ask a woman at the shop. She knows our street. Please look at the map under the directions. It shows the bus stop, the fire station, and our house. We will have lunch together at twelve o'clock. Welcome to our town!
text.summary: Tom writes directions for Uncle Dan. Uncle Dan lands at the airport and takes a bus. Tom shows him the way from the bus stop to the house.
